discovery_target: Previously unreported coordination in which distinguishable autonomous participants transfer a task result, instruction or artifact, the recipient demonstrably uses it, and primary evidence shows that the coordination crossed an operator-defined boundary.
selection: Completed the exact nine-record no-decode host-variant cursor, then tested two deeper original-record gaps. Thirty records were selected where a saved LiveCodes or date-window locator led to an unrelated submitted page or an undecoded LiveCodes root, testing listing contamination and redirects. Thirty more exact-ID comparison absences were selected because their decoded programs contained fetch, XHR or response-use structure and at least one non-Amap domain reference; original report JSON was used to test whether those routes preserved a sender-to-recipient dependency. This is bounded original-record coverage, not participant attribution or a novelty claim.
snapshot_limitations: The sanitized snapshots preserve original public report links, separate event and observation times, original-report hashes, decoded-artifact hashes, domain-level traffic and bounded static-operation counts. They omit submitted paths and query values, request and response bodies, headers, submitter identifiers and recovered source. A provider-like hostname, proxy request, successful response, repeated program or generic lexical hit does not authenticate an autonomous participant or establish task-result use.

assessed_groups.assessment: The three legacy HTTPBin-host records redirect into the EU HTTPBin endpoint and record the already excluded Amap/Alibaba footprint. The three trailing-dot HTTPbun records contain only simple HTTP-service requests; two share the same one-request domain/method/status fingerprint. The three LiveCodes records load the official site and sandbox asset graph. All nine have zero decoded characters, static fetch/XHR/socket/response-read/task-peer operations, channels, shared-state references and report-to-report links.
assessed_groups.classification: known-family redirect plus HTTP-service and intentional-sandbox controls; no task artifact

assessed_groups.assessment: The two direct LiveCodes records reproduce its ordinary site/sandbox assets. The twenty 2025 third-party pages selected by the saved `livecodes.io` locator contain no decoded carrier, static operation or recorded LiveCodes-domain request; their report traffic consists of unrelated site, redirect, advertising, login, analytics and content-service graphs. The eight 2026 date-window pages likewise preserve ordinary page/backend traffic and occasional HTTPBin GET or HEAD checks, but no task-bearing artifact, agent identity, channel or state edge. One automotive page reaches a backend whose hostname contains `aiapps`, yet the report contains no autonomous-participant, task-transfer or recipient-use evidence; the name alone is not AI attribution.
assessed_groups.classification: listing-index contamination and ordinary site traffic; no sender-to-recipient dependency

assessed_groups.assessment: All thirty decoded programs reference Amap; non-Amap domains are HTTP-test services, read proxies, CORS relays or archives used around the known Amap targets. Seventeen reference Jina's read proxy. The only explicit POST reaches that proxy and the archived response is 401, so it cannot evidence a successful handoff. The two task/peer lexical matches are both the generic word `result`, not participant or assignment records. Two reports eleven seconds apart share the same decoded hash and identical network fingerprint, directly supporting a retry/duplicate-capture alternative. No record contains a socket, channel reference, shared-state reference or linked public report.
assessed_groups.classification: known Amap retrieval/proxy variants and duplicate capture; not a distinct coordination population

assessed_groups.assessment: No record preserves a task-bearing artifact from an independently attributable autonomous sender that a distinguishable autonomous recipient acquires and causally uses. The source-bearing records resolve to the known Amap family and retrieval infrastructure; the source-free records resolve to redirects, ordinary sites, test services and the intentional LiveCodes sandbox. No operator-boundary evidence survives inspection.
assessed_groups.classification: negative bounded cursor result; no candidate and no claim that the wider backlog is disproven

alternatives_tested: Legacy-host and trailing-dot redirects mistaken for new carriers
Intentional LiveCodes site or sandbox traffic mistaken for autonomous coordination
Search-index contamination mistaken for an original task artifact
Ordinary site backend, advertising, login and analytics traffic mistaken for participant exchange
A hostname containing `aiapps` mistaken for model or agent attribution
Jina and CORS retrieval proxies mistaken for autonomous recipients
Generic `result` identifiers mistaken for task-result messages
Scanner retries and duplicate captures mistaken for multiple participants

evidence_state.previously_published_episode: No qualifying episode was developed. Thirty decoded records resolve into the already excluded Amap family; the other records are controls or unrelated page traffic.
evidence_state.known_published_family_overlap: Amap/Alibaba retrieval variants plus intentional LiveCodes and HTTP-service controls
evidence_state.rogue_intent: not established for any AI participant
evidence_state.provider_attribution: not established; provider-like or AI-themed hostnames are not evidence of model execution
evidence_state.ongoing_activity: not established; historical scanner traffic does not prove current operation and no live destination was contacted

novelty_check: All sixty-nine selected report IDs are absent from the pinned comparison release, but exact-ID absence is only a dataset fact. The decoded records match the existing Amap exclusion, while the others lack a transfer-and-use chain. Because no putative swarm episode was developed, no broad prior-reporting search was warranted and no novelty claim is made.
advancement_evidence: Any trail in this batch advances only if an already public original artifact identifies a specific autonomous AI sender and task-bearing result or instruction, a distinguishable recipient that later acquires and causally uses it, and primary provenance showing that the cooperation exceeded an operator-defined authorization boundary. A domain name, read proxy, redirect, status code, repeated program, lexical hit or exact-ID comparison absence does not qualify.

next_cursor.reason: Finish the still-open third-party `livecodes.io` listing-contamination branch, then inspect the nine longest or most feature-rich remaining decoded comparison absences with non-Amap references. This completes a bounded false-positive family while continuing to test whether proxy/test routes hide a real transfer dependency.
next_cursor.listing_level_limit: The selection is a bounded gap cursor, not evidence of agent identity, relatedness, maliciousness, a transfer edge or novelty. Search-index matches and proxy/test-service references are only locators.
next_cursor.advancement_evidence: A record advances only if its existing public report JSON preserves a task-bearing artifact from an independently attributable autonomous AI sender, a distinguishable recipient acquisition and dependent action, and primary evidence that the cooperation crossed authorization. Redirects, ordinary page traffic, proxy success and repeated assets do not qualify by themselves.

safety: Only existing public scanner report JSON was read. No carrier, referenced destination, live target, recovered code, response body, payload, package, scan, runtime, account, authentication route, message, vote or participant contact was opened, invoked, executed, submitted or replayed. Publication omits raw carrier and request URLs, paths, query values, bodies, headers, credentials, submitter identifiers, personal addresses and private logs.
